title: The natural module short exact sequence of a binary subterminal cover
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ subterminal objects with $\{U,V\}\to1$ covering; put $W=U\times V$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], localized restrictions $j_Z^*$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and their extension-by-zero left adjoints $j_{Z!}F=P_F^\#$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], for $Z=U,V,W$. For an $R$-module sheaf $F$, let $\epsilon_Z:j_{Z!}j_Z^*F\to F$ be the adjunction counit. Define $i_U:j_{W!}j_W^*F\to j_{U!}j_U^*F$ as the $j_{W!}\dashv j_W^*$ transpose of the restriction to $W$ of the unit $j_U^*F\to j_U^*j_{U!}j_U^*F$, using canonical iterated restriction; define $i_V$ likewise. Then $\epsilon_U i_U=\epsilon_V i_V=\epsilon_W$ and
$$0\longrightarrow j_{W!}j_W^*F\xrightarrow{(i_U,-i_V)}j_{U!}j_U^*F\oplus j_{V!}j_V^*F\xrightarrow{(\epsilon_U,\epsilon_V)}F\longrightarrow0$$
is a short exact sequence, natural in $F$. Under the canonical restriction/extension intersection identifications, on $U$ it is
$$0\to L\xrightarrow{(i,-1)}F|_U\oplus L\xrightarrow{(1,i)}F|_U\to0,\qquad L=k_{U!}(F|_W),$$
and on $V$ it is
$$0\to L'\xrightarrow{(1,-i')}L'\oplus F|_V\xrightarrow{(i',1)}F|_V\to0,\qquad L'=k_{V!}(F|_W),$$
where $k_U:W\to U,k_V:W\to V$ denote the nested localizations and $i,i'$ their counits. Applied termwise to a cochain complex $K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], these maps commute with the differentials and give a degreewise short exact sequence natural in cochain maps.

proof.text: Put $A_Z(F)=j_{Z!}j_Z^*F$. Use the additive adjunctions and restriction identifications of [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus]. In particular $j_U^*A_U(F)=F|_U$ and $j_U^*A_V(F)=k_{U!}(F|_W)$. Also $j_U^*A_W(F)=k_{U!}(F|_W)$: on an object $C\to U$, the presheaf defining the left side before sheafification is $F(C)$ if $C\to W$ exists and zero otherwise. This is exactly the presheaf defining the right side, with the same restriction maps and $R(C)$-action, by [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and the relocalization of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Restriction commutes with this sheafification by the cited local-calculus statement, so the equality of presheaves gives the canonical sheaf identification. Interchanging $U$ and $V$ gives $j_V^*A_V(F)=F|_V$ and $j_V^*A_U(F)=j_V^*A_W(F)=k_{V!}(F|_W)$.

proof.text: Write $\eta_Z$ for the unit of $j_{Z!}\dashv j_Z^*$. By the definition of transpose, the image of $i_U$ under this adjunction for $W$ is $k_U^*\eta_U(F|_U)$, after the sectionwise iterated-restriction identifications. Postcomposition with $\epsilon_U(F)$ therefore gives transpose $j_W^*\epsilon_U(F)\circ k_U^*\eta_U(F|_U)=k_U^*(j_U^*\epsilon_U(F)\circ\eta_U(F|_U))=1_{F|_W}$, by the right triangle identity. The transpose of $\epsilon_W(F)$ is also $1_{F|_W}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $\epsilon_U i_U=\epsilon_W$. The identical computation with $V$ proves $\epsilon_V i_V=\epsilon_W$. Thus the proposed consecutive arrows compose to $\epsilon_W-\epsilon_W=0$. Only the adjunctions supplied by [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] and their defining identities are used.

source.place: Tag 08BU, lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek, proof: short exact sequence of complexes (agent generalization to subterminal slices, replacing stalks by the two local split calculations).

proof.text: Let $L=k_{U!}(F|_W)$ and let $i:L\to F|_U$ be its counit. Restrict the sequence to $U$ and use step 1. The unit identifications and their compatibility with counits and nested-open adjunction maps in [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] send $\epsilon_U$ to $1$, $\epsilon_V$ to $i$, $i_U$ to $i$, and $i_V$ to $1_L$. For the last two assertions, the restricted transpose defining the nested-open map is respectively the identity of $F|_W$ under $k_{U!}\dashv k_U^*$, and the unit transpose of the identity of $L$; hence these are precisely the counit $i$ and the identity. Consequently the restricted arrows are $(i,-1)$ and $(1,i)$. On $V$, writing $L^{\prime}=k_{V!}(F|_W)$ and $i^{\prime}:L^{\prime}\to F|_V$ for its counit, the same compatibility sends $i_U$ to $1_{L^{\prime}}$, $i_V$ to $i^{\prime}$, and the counits to $i^{\prime}$ and $1$. The restricted arrows are therefore $(1,-i^{\prime})$ and $(i^{\prime},1)$, with exactly the signs asserted in the statement.

proof.text: The local sequences of step 3 are split short exact by direct module calculations. On $U$ set $a(x)=(i(x),-x)$, $b(y,z)=y+i(z)$, $s(y)=(y,0)$ and $r(y,z)=-z$. Then $ba=0$, $ra=1$, $bs=1$, and $ar+sb=1$: indeed $ar(y,z)=(-i(z),z)$ and $sb(y,z)=(y+i(z),0)$. These equations show that $a$ is monic, $b$ is epic, and that every morphism $t$ killed by $b$ factors uniquely as $a(rt)$; hence $a$ is the kernel of $b$. On $V$ take $a^{\prime}(x)=(x,-i^{\prime}(x))$, $b^{\prime}(y,z)=i^{\prime}(y)+z$, $s^{\prime}(z)=(0,z)$ and $r^{\prime}(y,z)=y$. The same four equations hold, since $a^{\prime}r^{\prime}(y,z)=(y,-i^{\prime}(y))$ and $s^{\prime}b^{\prime}(y,z)=(0,i^{\prime}(y)+z)$. All formulas are module-linear sheaf maps in the abelian module categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; they do not require the local counits $i,i^{\prime}$ to be isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply the joint detection of exactness by $(j_U^*,j_V^*)$ in [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] to the entire sequence with zero endpoints. Both restrictions are short exact by step 4, so the sequence on $\mathcal E$ is exact at every term, including injectivity at $A_W(F)$ and surjectivity at $F$. The covering and small-site hypotheses are exactly those of that cited statement. No hypothesis that the topos has enough points is used.

source.place: Tag 08BU, lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek, proof: short exact sequence of complexes (agent generalization to subterminal slices, replacing stalks by the two local split calculations).

proof.text: For a module map $h:F\to G$, let $A_Z(h)=j_{Z!}j_Z^*h$. Naturality of the adjunction counit gives $h\epsilon_Z(F)=\epsilon_Z(G)A_Z(h)$. The equality $A_U(h)i_U(F)=i_U(G)A_W(h)$ follows by taking $W$-transposes: it becomes $j_W^*A_U(h)\,k_U^*\eta_U(F|_U)=k_U^*\eta_U(G|_U)\,j_W^*h$, which is the restriction of the naturality identity for $\eta_U$. The same argument applies to $i_V$. Thus both arrows of the sequence are natural in $F$. The additive functors in [lem-sp-subterminal-module-local-calculus] act on a cochain complex termwise. Apply these naturality equations to $h=d_K^r$ to see that $(i_U,-i_V)$ and $(\epsilon_U,\epsilon_V)$ commute with every differential. Functoriality sends $d_K^{r+1}d_K^r=0$ to zero, so these are complexes and maps in the sense of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 5 applied to each $K^r$ gives degreewise short exactness. Applied to the components of a cochain map, the same equations give the asserted naturality in cochain maps.
